correctness.rationale: Expanding the exact survival at \(v=(\lambda/(\lambda+x))^\theta=0\) gives a positive regularly varying tail with exponent \(-\theta\) and explicit constant. The density has exponent \(-\theta-1\), and the hazard satisfies \(x h(x)\to\theta\). The tail integral criterion then proves \(\mathbb E[X^q]<\infty\) if and only if \(q<\theta\), including logarithmic divergence at \(q=\theta\). The same lower-tail comparison with \(e^{tx}\) proves divergence of \(\mathbb E[e^{tX}]\) for every \(t>0\). A standalone checker was replayed from the embedded package path and agrees with all asymptotic constants.

value.rationale: Moments, variance, and the MGF are presented by the target as fundamental mathematical properties of a new heavy-tailed model. The theorem gives the complete sharp positive-moment domain, quantifies critical and supercritical divergence, and shows that an ordinary MGF does not exist at all. These facts materially change how the printed formulas can be used and establish that the added flexibility parameter does not alter tail order.
